subject: Request: One-off credit for overage during pilot (follow-up & accounting plan)
content:
From: Maya Lewis <maya@oceanic.energy>
To: jonas_weber@redwood.ai
Cc: accounts@oceanic.energy
Date: Tue, 1 Jul 2025 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Quick: pilot overage / request for one-off credit

Hi Jonas,

Thanks again — our pilot wrapped last week and we pulled a lot more tokens than expected. Can Redwood issue a one-time credit to offset the invoice you sent for June? We don't want this to block our procurement sign-off while execs finish the PO.

Attached is a short note from our PM showing the spike and the pilot usage export. If possible we'd prefer a credit memo applied to the open invoice (INV-2049) rather than a separate refund.

Appreciate any quick guidance — Maya

Attachments: oceanic_request.pdf (PDF) | trial_usage_report.csv (CSV)

---
From: Jonas Weber <jonas_weber@redwood.ai>
To: Maya Lewis <maya@oceanic.energy>
Cc: Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.ai>, Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.ai>, Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa_ortiz@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 1 Jul 2025 09:34:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Quick: pilot overage / request for one-off credit

Thanks Maya — looping in Finance (Marcus) and RevOps (Laura, Vanessa) for accounting treatment and to confirm next steps.

High level: we can issue a customer credit memo that offsets INV-2049, but need accounting confirmation on GLA and whether to treat this as a promotional allowance or contra-revenue (per Redwood policy).

Marcus/Laura/V: please advise on journal treatment and whether we should record as an immediately-posted credit memo or hold in a suspense account until PO converts. Also flag any doc/approval you need from Oceanic.

Jonas

---
From: Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.ai>
To: jonas_weber@redwood.ai, laura_bennett@redwood.ai, vanessa_ortiz@redwood.ai
Date: Tue, 1 Jul 2025 10:05:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Quick: pilot overage / request for one-off credit

Jonas — thanks. I reviewed the usage file. Amount in question is $14,230 (post-tax not included). Two options:

1) Credit memo against INV-2049 and post as contra-revenue (GLA 4002) — cleans receivables and reduces recognized revenue. This is simplest operationally.
2) Record as a promotional allowance (GLA 5308) and move to a promo suspense account until commercial outcome (PO signed) — keeps revenue intact but requires a reversing entry if PO converts.

Accounting prefers option (1) when the credit is requested to clear an outstanding invoice and doesn't carry conditions. If Oceanic explicitly ties the credit to a future committed contract, we should consider (2).

Also: we need an authorization e-mail from a Oceanic finance contact and LR approval for >$10k credits (Laura). If RevOps wants a holdback, we can do a temporary allowance then reclassify.

Marcus

---
From: Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.ai>
To: Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.ai>, jonas_weber@redwood.ai, vanessa_ortiz@redwood.ai
Date: Tue, 1 Jul 2025 11:12:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Quick: pilot overage / request for one-off credit

Marcus — per policy and the customer's ask, I approve option (1): issue a credit memo, post as contra-revenue GLA 4002, and offset INV-2049. This avoids keeping a lingering liability and aligns with standard invoice-netting.

Please prepare the credit memo draft and route to legal for a quick sign-off (cc me). Marcus, please confirm the journal entry format (we'll need JE and allocation details). Vanessa, can you coordinate posting and notify CS and the customer once complete?

Laura Bennett
Director, RevOps
Redwood Inference
